guides.title: Android Auto doesn't start
guides.summary: The phone is plugged in or nearby, but Android Auto doesn't appear on the car's screen.
symptoms: android auto not showing on the screen
phone screen not showing on the car display

steps.text: Check that your car supports Android Auto and that it is switched on in the car's settings (often under Smartphone connection).
Park the car, unlock the phone, and accept the Android Auto messages on both the phone and the car's screen.
steps.detail: The first setup only works with the car standing still.

steps.text: Do you connect with a cable or wirelessly?
Use the data USB port (often marked with a phone symbol) and a short original data cable.
Update Android Auto, Google Maps and Google Play services from the Play Store.
Switch on both Bluetooth and Wi-Fi on the phone, and switch off its mobile hotspot.
steps.detail: Wireless Android Auto uses Bluetooth to start and Wi-Fi to carry the picture.

steps.text: Forget the car in Bluetooth and in Android Auto's settings, then set it up again; some cars need one connection with a cable first.
In Android Auto's settings, remove the car from 'Previously connected cars' and connect again.
Restart the phone, and restart the car's system: car off, locked, wait 5 minutes.

escalate.text: The car's media system may need a software update for your phone.
tell_service: Phone model, Android version and Android Auto version
Cable or wireless, and which cable
Any message on the car's screen or the phone

guides.title: Apple CarPlay doesn't start
guides.summary: The iPhone is plugged in or nearby, but CarPlay doesn't appear on the car's screen.
symptoms: carplay not showing on the screen
iphone not connecting to the car screen

steps.text: On the iPhone, open Settings > General > CarPlay and check your car is listed and allowed.
Check that Screen Time doesn't block CarPlay (Settings > Screen Time > Content & Privacy Restrictions > Allowed Apps) and that Siri is on.
Do you connect with a cable or wirelessly?
Use the car's data USB port and an Apple or certified cable; unlock the iPhone and tap Allow or Trust.
Switch on Bluetooth and Wi-Fi, switch off Personal Hotspot and airplane mode, then in Settings > General > CarPlay choose your car > Forget This Car and set it up again.
Restart the iPhone, and restart the car's system: car off, locked, wait 5 minutes.

escalate.text: The car's media system may need a software update.
tell_service: Any message on the car's screen

guides.title: Android Auto or CarPlay keeps disconnecting
guides.summary: The phone's apps disappear from the screen while driving and come back, or the connection is lost.
symptoms: screen goes back to the car menu
android auto baar baar band ho jata hai

steps.text: Replace the cable with a short (under 1 metre) data cable, without adapters or extension cables.
steps.detail: A worn or long cable is the most common cause.

steps.text: Keep the phone out of direct sun and off a wireless charger while it's connected.
steps.detail: Phones drop the connection when they get too hot.

steps.text: Look for lint in the phone's port and check the cable sits firmly.
Switch off battery saver, and update the phone and Android Auto or iOS.
For wireless: keep the phone near the screen, and make sure no other phone is connected to the car.

escalate.text: The car's USB connection or media system may need a check.
tell_service: Cable or wireless, and which phone
Whether it happens with another phone or cable
